pool.text: A Portuguese fort was destroyed by local inhabitants living in the area.
A dispute escalated to a military conflict when Accra invaded Larteh.
Akwamuhene Ansa Sasraku attacked Accra using a visiting prince's circumcision as pretext.
Ansa Sasraku returned to burn Osu town and Small Accra while chasing Ofori.
Britain began acquiring interests by buying Christiansborg and other forts from Denmark.
The Netherlands became the final country to sell out their colonial interests.
The British captured Accra following earlier conflicts with the Ashantis.
Accra officially replaced Cape Coast to serve as the British Gold Coast capital.
The geographical boundaries of Accra were stretched following a bubonic plague epidemic.
Achimota School, also known as Motown, opened its doors to students.
Ghana remained a colony of Great Britain following the events of World War II.
Ghana International School was founded in Cantonments for children aged three to eighteen.
Kwame Nkrumah became the first Prime Minister and created a development plan.
Lincoln Community School was established in Abelemkpe as a private international school.
The World Bank estimated the local economy contributed three billion dollars to GDP.
The primary school enrollment rate in the city reached ninety-five percent.
International tourist arrivals in Ghana reached over one million visitors.
A scientific study determined city greenspaces are important for local mammal biodiversity.
The think tank designated the territory as a Gamma minus level global city.
The very first documentary addressing climate change impacts premiered in the city.
